newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China says no change on oil product tariff system.
newsitem.headline: China says no change on oil product tariff system.

text.p: China has no plan to change its tariff system on oil product imports after it applies a new system on crude oil imports in July, a Chinese customs official said on Monday.
Currently China imposes tariffs on crude oil and oil products according to the value of the imports.
But starting July 1, China has said it would implement a special import tariff of 16 yuan ($1.90) per tonne on crude oil, replacing a current tariff of 1.5 percent on the value of the import.

"We have no plan to apply the crude oil tariff system on oil products. Tariffs on products will still be value-based but not quantity-based," the official at the State Council's Customs Office said from Beijing.
China currently imposes 6-12 percent tariffs on oil product imports, the official said.
China has said it would impose six percent tariffs on the value of fuel oil and gas oil imports starting April 1, replacing current 12 percent and three percent respectively.
